What does zone VE mean?

Zone VE is a coastal high-risk area: land with a 1 percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year, hit by tidal floods with fast-moving water, where FEMA has worked out how high the water would reach (44 CFR §59.1, §64.3).

Am I required to buy flood insurance?

Federal law requires it only in a high-risk zone (A or V) with a federally regulated or backed mortgage, or federal help to buy or build (42 U.S.C. §4012a). Outside them, a lender can still require it.

What does it cost in zone VE, by state?

Since FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0, price is set from each building's own flood risk, not its zone, and these are existing policies whose buildings differ. The reason for any one zone is not in this data.

Most insured units in this zone are not in the median: 148,995 units are rated VE, while the median above rests on 18,640 single-family primary-home policies.

How do I get covered?

Most policies start 30 days after you buy, but there is no wait if you buy it with a new or refinanced mortgage. To buy: call the NFIP at (877) 336-2627, go to FloodSmart.gov, or ask any licensed insurance agent. Every NFIP insurer offers the same rates.

What this page cannot tell you

Your premium, private insurers' prices, your exact zone, why prices rise, and claims paid in this exact zone across the country. FEMA's map and an agent's quote answer those for your address.
